blocking.what: The in-scope rule picks code by whether a law reads it. Rollup.sol is limited to the 25 functions and modifiers reached from the 8 actions the M1 abstraction models. The M2 diagram's extracted rollup model and its coverage record span the whole contract, so the operator sites in the other extracted actions are left out of the denominator without being reported.
blocking.why: This selects on a variable tied to the outcome: a site no law reads cannot be killed. That biases the kill rate upward against HOLON's real sensitivity on the code it certifies. Whitepaper §9.5 names 'rule gap' as an expected A1 miss. §12.1 has certificates report Sensitivity alongside Coverage over the same in-scope code. Under this rule, every rule-gap miss of the kind 'no law covers this action' is excluded by construction. The lead's delegated Q8 answer (docs/HUMAN_ANSWERS.md) calls a hand-picked subset a selection bias, and the standing guidance is to take the stricter option. Size: 11 more mutants, about 10% of the denominator, and probably all survivors, against a 0.80 threshold.

advisory.what:
About 24 of the 110 mutants cannot be killed by construction under the frozen law sets and kill criterion, and the catalog does not say so.

- drop_delete M035–M040 and swap_cursor M041–M048 (14 mutants). Their only predicted laws are M1x laws. M1x's decided input (law_sets.M1x, line 1111) is m1_view: the hand abstraction minus the requires of guard_missing deltas. guard_missing is matched by line span (tests_m2/test_extracted_refinement.py:30), and the unmerged I20-A holon/differential.py says 'no other delta changes the view'. No operator removes a require, and every rewrite keeps line numbers, so m1_view stays byte-identical and M1x statuses are carried. Separately, L_undo_BVH, L_undo_cancel and L_sym_omega are REFUTED in results/M1, and two of them are predicted REFUTED on the extracted model (UNDO_KEPT, test_extracted_refinement.py:89).
- M037–M040 also differ only in storage residue that public getters read. The UNDO laws exclude getters by design (laws/M1/L_undo_BD.json notes), while the equivalence definition counts every storage slot.
- shl_width M031–M034, the dataHash preimage in Rollup._commitBatch. enc_sol takes dataHash as an input Header field: in morph_header.extracted.json the ops have src 'field dataHash', and the keccak sink at Rollup.sol:883 has selected: false. The normalized projected document is therefore unchanged, and M0 is carried.
- drop_len_check M107–M110, and cmp_boundary M049 and M063. The only law that reads ok_sol or ok_go on arbitrary bytes is L_dom_hdr, which is REFUTED at baseline (results/M0, law_sets.M0.baseline_committed), so not_kills applies. L_rt_go_* only apply ok_go to enc_sol outputs, which are exactly 249 or 257 bytes with a valid version, so dropping a length check cannot change them.
advisory.why: This is not bias: each case reflects a real HOLON blind spot or the plan's verbatim criterion. But part of the outcome is fixed before anything runs. On this reading the maximum is 86 kills. If 2 equivalent mutants fall outside these 24, then 5·86 = 430 < 4·108 = 432 and the threshold is missed. It becomes reachable only if at least 3 of these 24 are adjudicated equivalent and every other mutant is killed. Record each mutant's structural class in the catalog before freezing, so survivors are attributed mechanically (window view, refuted law, abstracted field), not after the fact. Caveat: I20 is not merged on this branch. The M1x argument rests on the prereg's own law_sets text, the I20 test docstring and the I20-A worktree code.

blocking.what: K2 (PROVED to UNKNOWN on a changed set input) counts proof losses that are not localized obstructions. Four routes let a law that is still true on the mutant code score as a kill: set-level attribution, in-run checker timeouts, emitter Unsupported, and dirty-memory undefinedness.
blocking.why: The plan's head clause is 'killed iff the obstruction predicted for its operator appears, localized to the mutated edge'. Whitepaper §12.1 L1 defines sensitivity as a real defect surfacing as an obstruction, and L15 forbids reading proof failure as a counterexample. K2 also contradicts the prereg's own error clause, which says a checker timeout is an error. The stakes are decisive: sound kills alone cannot reach the threshold (see advisory 1), so K2's looseness is one of only two ways the 0.80 threshold could be met.
blocking.evidence: (1) Set level, not law level. kill_criterion.K2 (prereg JSON line 1126) tests 'the normalized decided input of the law's set'. In the M2 set, the 6 PROVED SORT-site laws read only spec/M1/facts/morph_rollup.json, which no mutant changes; their decisions use only the hand model, since re-extraction evidence enters only the site-spec hash (I20 branch holon/sorts/sites.py:282,400; holon/sorts/reextract.py docstring: 'The statement itself is unchanged'). Yet the set input changes for every Solidity mutant, through the width laws' spec/M2/facts/morph_rollup.extracted.json. Under cmp_boundary 'any', any proof loss of those 6 laws therefore counts. (2) Timeouts and Unsupported. holon/bend.py:284-286 turns subprocess.TimeoutExpired (180 s wall clock, config/holon.json bend.timeout_s) into Run(code=None). holon/pipeline.py:89-95 and 177-200, and holon/mpipeline.py:663-665, record that as a failed attempt and end the law UNKNOWN with exit 0. LG.Unsupported likewise becomes UNKNOWN (pipeline.py:194-200). The prereg's error clause (line 1129) calls a timeout an error but says nothing about how a timeout inside holon run is detected, so as written K2 counts it. (3) M018 (storeSequencerSetVerifyHash mstore at 186). Header byte 185 is never written. The model starts encoder buffers as UNDEF (holon/gen/model.py:190), and the refuter never accepts an undefined value as a witness (holon/refute.py:128-131,154,171; holon/model_eval.py:106-111). So L_par_hdr_v0/v1 and L_rt_go_v0/v1/v2 can be neither proved nor refuted: 5 K2 'kills'. On the code that byte is fresh EVM memory, equal to Go's 0 under the ssvh=0 premise, so all five claims are plausibly still true. (4) drop_len_check (M107-M110). L_dom_hdr is the only law that applies ok_go to arbitrary bytes, and it is baseline REFUTED. L_rt_go_v0..v2 apply ok_go/dec_go only to enc_sol outputs, which always have the version's exact length (249/257) and are non-empty, so all three stay true on M107-M110. Any kill for this operator could only be a K2 proof loss on a true law.
blocking.fix: Replace K2 with: baseline PROVED, mutant UNKNOWN, and all three of: (a) the law's own decided input changed, meaning its statement, the facts documents it names, and the kernel forms of its cone (holon.bindings.kernel_cone, already recorded in results/<M>/deps.json); a law whose own input is identical is carried. (b) The generator that proved the law in the baseline ran to completion on the mutant and Bend rejected the proof (non-null exit code, marker 'SOME PROOFS FAIL'). A timeout (exit_code null or '[timeout]'), LG.Unsupported, or a generator returning None is a law-level error, retried once, and never K2. (c) A code-level localized falsification exists: some input in the law's deterministic candidate space, in refuter order and at most replay_candidates of them, shows the claim false on the mutant code and not on the unmutated code. A proof loss that meets (a) and (b) but not (c) is recorded as proof_lost_unwitnessed, not as a kill. (a) and (b) are the minimum needed to agree with 'localized to the mutated edge' and with the prereg's own error clause. (c) is what makes a proof loss an obstruction. It keeps every legitimate K2 kill (M078 panics, M017/M020/M022 unwritten-plus-shifted bytes) and drops M018-type kills. Also report the K1-only kill count next to the official rate.

blocking.what: The error clause lets an infrastructure failure on any law set, or on any law's witness replay (including laws outside the predicted set), turn a mutant into 'error' (not killed) even when a predicted law already satisfies K1.
blocking.why: This contradicts the plan's 'killed iff the obstruction predicted for its operator appears' and biases the rate downward. The bias is uneven: Solidity mutants depend on three law sets plus replays, Go mutants only on M0.
blocking.evidence: kill_criterion.error (line 1129): 'a step of the decision path (source, extraction, a law set, a witness replay) that fails ... if it fails again the mutant's outcome is error, which counts as not killed'. kill_criterion.replay (line 1131) requires a replay for every law that moves to REFUTED, predicted or not. Concrete paths: holon derive refuses on a stale site assignment (holon/rules/__init__.py:181 Refused; holon/sorts/sites.py:389 StaleSites). An unpredicted M2 width law moving to REFUTED needs a replay harness that does not exist. Either one would erase a valid L_par_hdr_v0 K1 kill on an mstore_offset mutant.
blocking.fix: Scope errors to laws. A failed step marks only the laws it decides, or the law whose witness it replays, as error (undecided). A mutant is killed iff some predicted law satisfies K1/K2 on a path that completed. Its outcome is error iff it is not killed and some predicted law is undecided because of an error. Failures on unpredicted laws and on channels are recorded only. Report error counts per step.

advisory.what: The replay panic/error rule conflicts with the declared function meanings and is undefined for trace laws.
advisory.why: 'Returns an error where the claim needs its value makes the claim false' contradicts ok_go ('true iff validate() returns nil'), ok_sol ('true iff _loadBatchHeader does not revert') and dec_go ('None if validate() fails'), where the error or revert is the value. Read literally, L_dom_hdr is false at every input Go rejects. For M1x/M2 trace laws, a reverted step is a no-op, not a violation. The model never accepts an undefined value as a witness, while the code replay counts a panic as falsifying, so panicking mutants such as M078 can die only through K2.
advisory.fix: Map errors and reverts through each function's facts meaning. Apply the panic rule only to panics the meaning does not map. For trace laws, use Solidity panic codes at the law's site (the I15 panic_site replay).

advisory.what: Determinism checks lack a stated consequence.
advisory.why: 'run --check decides every set and must agree' does not say what happens if it disagrees. The 180 s Bend timeout is the only wall-clock budget in the pipeline (explorer budgets are node counts).
advisory.fix: Treat a --check disagreement as an error for the affected laws, and report it.
